source_text: Okay, well it very clearly is a stopgap measure because the way the patterns are stored, Is in a library in the Futon 3 Library and they're also replicated in XTDB but even more importantly I've been creating a connected, giant connected pattern Cascade of all the patterns that have been used and attested and linked together and having a separate file that gives feedback that's distinct from that cascade is a mistake so I think the first thing we should do is find the giant connected cascade and then think about what feedback looks like relative to that cascade, because that cascade is the repository of learning about patterns and learning about how patterns connect to each other and so if we wanted to attribute some success to some pattern or another that is selected and used in a specific cascade, you By the War Machine then we should probably do that attestation relative to the a giant connected component.

reply_text:
Found the graph; doing one last check of whether the last click actually read it, then reporting.㊥ ("find the giant connected cascade") I found a graph that matches your description, and I need you to confirm it is the one you mean. The War Machine's click does not read it, and nothing from a War Machine run is written into it. I have set the click request aside until the feedback question is settled against this graph.

㊢ (where it is)
- **File:** `/home/joe/code/storage/operator-turns/mined-pattern-graph.json`, last written 1 October.
- **Generator:** `futon3c/scripts/mined_pattern_graph.py`, which can rebuild it at any time from its sources.
- **Size:** 1,431 library patterns, 4,552 links, built from 5,816 analysed operator turns.
- **Connected part:** 734 patterns in the largest component with all link kinds, 660 without the weakest kind; 421 patterns have no links.

㊢ (what the links are) Every link carries its kind and the evidence for it:

| Kind | Count | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `why` | 545 | written in the library pattern |
| `how` | 90 | written in the library pattern |
| `co-cited` | 855 | two patterns cited in one of your turns |
| `rejected-beside` | 338 | one pattern turned down where another was cited |
| `next-in-session` | 2,724 | patterns cited in consecutive turns |

So the graph records where patterns were cited together in your turns and how the library relates them. It has no record of a pattern being used in a click, or of what the click achieved.

㊩ (the War Machine side)
- **Readers exist but are not called.** futon2 has three modules that load this graph and cut cascades out of it, with tests. Nothing in the click runner calls them.
- **The last click did not use it.** Its run record has no reference to the graph.
- **Its four patterns:** three are in the connected part; `ukrns/reader-run-path` has no links at all.

🈳 (not checked) I did not look at the copy in XTDB, so I cannot say whether it holds the same links or more.

㊭ ("what feedback looks like relative to that cascade") A first sketch, for you to correct:
1. **A click becomes one more source for the generator**, beside the turn analyses. The separate feedback file goes away.
2. **Per pattern:** the click adds evidence of the form "used in run R for want W, and the want was reached, progressed or untouched".
3. **Per pair of patterns in the chosen cascade:** the click adds a link of a new kind, "used together in run R", keeping the order they were applied in and the outcome.
4. **Selection reads the graph.** If the habit term is to prefer patterns that worked, it takes those counts from the graph's evidence.

That way a click's result sits in the same place, and in the same form, as the rest of what is known about how patterns connect.

🈯 ("giant connected pattern cascade") Is this file the cascade you mean, or is the one you have been building somewhere else, for example in XTDB?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("it isn't something I asked to have created") You are right on both points: I found no request of yours behind this mechanism, and "start from an empty file" was housekeeping that I should not have put to you as a decision. I withdraw that question. Below is what the mechanism is and what I propose in its place.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
("what it's actually supposed to implement") It is meant to make the machine prefer patterns that worked before, across clicks. It works in two steps:
1. **After a click:** the machine appends one record to a file, listing the patterns in the chosen cascade and whether each is credited.
2. **Before the next selection:** it reads every record in the file and counts the credits per pattern. A candidate cascade that contains credited patterns has its habit weight multiplied up, so it is more likely to be chosen again.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (where it came from) codex-10 added it on 1 October in four commits; one of them was dispatched by claude-17. I looked at the commit messages and at the notes under `futon2/holes` and `docs`, and found no ruling or note asking for it. I did not search further than that.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("at best, a stopgap measure") The file currently holds seven records from 1–4 October, written before the machine measured wants at all. Five of them give credit, and the next selection will still count those. By "empty file" I meant setting those seven aside so the next click starts with no credits. That would only tidy the inputs of a mechanism whose place in the machine is itself undecided.
